To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pituitary protein GnSIF/ AF governs the LH secretion rate during the follicular phase of the ovarian cycle, by neutralizing the effect of the self-priming of the pituitaries, and thereby prevents the premature reinitation of meiosis and ovulation.
the stabilization of low LH concentrations during the follicular phase is a prerequisite for optimal embryo quality.

the stabilization of low LH concentrations during the preovulatory period of the ovarian cycles is a prerequisite for optimal oocyte development and embryo viability and survival; the stabilization of low concentrations is accomplished by the interaction of the pituitaries' self-priming proteins with the ovarian protein GnSIF/ AF; and the antagonistic interaction between pituitary self-priming and GnSIF/A F provides a mode of action to control LH secretion during the ovarian cycles.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the mechanism underlying the self-priming phenomenon, the characterization of the self-primed proteins and their interaction with GnSIF/ AF, the identification of the molecular nature of GnSIF, and the elucidation of its mode of action.
the identification of GnRH-induced self-priming proteins, the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of their interaction with GnSIF/ AF and the characterization of GnSIF itself.

the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of the self-priming effect and the identification and characterization of the self- priming proteins, and the elucidation of their interaction with GnSIF/ AF.

GnSIF/ is a physiological regulator of gonadotrope responsiveness to GnRH.
GnSIF/ AF is a major factor that determines the LH secretion rate during the follicular phase of the ovarian cycle.
the GnSIF/ AF system is a key factor in the regulation of LH secretion during the ovarian cycles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the female, the ovarian cycle is controlled by a complex interaction of several hormones and factors that are released by the ovary, the pituitaries and the brain.
GnRH and GnSF/AF act in concert as a regulatory mechanism to maintain low LH concentrations during the follicular phase of the ovarian cycle.
the stabilization of low LH concentrations is a prerequisite for optimal oocyte maturation and survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stabilization of low LH concentrations during the period preceding the mid-cycle surge is of importance for embryo quality and viability.
the regulation of the LH release during the ovarian cycle is a dynamic process, which is governed by the balance between the stimulatory and inhibitory effects of GnRH and GnSI/AF.

the antagonistic interaction between the GnRH and GnRH-induced proteins, such as GnSIF/ AF, is an important factor in the control of the LH concentration during the ovulatory cycle and that the regulation of LH secretion is not only a matter of the GnRH pulse frequency, but also of the balance between the GnRH-induced self-priming and GnSIF/GnAF.
